qa.question: Should Germantown capacities follow the EIA nameplate or the DNR permit ratings?
qa.finding: The EIA-860M table for September 2026 gives 71.2 MW for Units 1 to 4 and 105.9 MW for Unit 5. The 2019 Wisconsin DNR permit at https://apps.dnr.wi.gov/warp_ext/AM_DownloadObject.aspx?id=859072 says Units 1 to 4 total 224 MW and Unit 5 is 85 MW.
qa.recommendation: Use the EIA nameplate figures, 71.2 MW for each of Units 1 to 4 and 105.9 MW for Unit 5, because GEM records nameplate capacity.
qa.note: In the permit, go to the equipment list near the start of the permit. The line starts 'Eight Simple Cycle Combustion Turbines arranged in pairs' and ends 'total electrical capacity of 224 MW'. The Unit 5 line ends 'total electric capacity of 85 MW'. The permit ratings are lower than EIA's nameplate, which is likely a site rating at permit conditions. Each of Units 1 to 4 is a pair of Pratt and Whitney turbines, per a 2024 DNR application, but I could not verify that page with the link checker because its text is spaced out, so I did not report it.
